about.label: Our Heritage
about.title: A Legacy Built on
about.notice: Ko Win Naing Electronic Service first opened in 1989 on Yadanar Road, at the 14–15 junction, 12 Quarter, South Okkalapa. The workshop has since moved to North Okkalapa, near Maydar Wee Market, and now serves under the name Sein Pan Electronic Service.
about.p1a: Sein Pan Electronic Service began from a belief that every broken television should be repaired at a fair and reasonable price. Founder
about.p1c: near the 14–15 junction in South Okkalapa, using the electronics skill he already had. As old and new customers grew, the shop moved to North Okkalapa around 2015 and has continued under the name Sein Pan Electronic.
about.p2: Over more than three decades, the shop evolved from servicing bulky CRT sets to mastering modern LED, LCD, and plasma technologies — always staying ahead of the curve while keeping that same neighbourhood warmth and trusted reputation.
about.p3b: , North Okkalapa township, the shop is more accessible than ever, continuing to serve Yangon families with the same dedication that built its 37-year legacy.

timeline.title: The Beginning
timeline.body: Ko Win Naing founded Sein Pan Electronic Service near the 14–15 junction, Yadanar Road, 12 Quarter, South Okkalapa — serving the neighbourhood with honest, skilled TV repair.

timeline.title: Growing Reputation
timeline.body: Word spread across Yangon. Customers from neighbouring townships sought Sein Pan specifically for their LCD and Plasma sets — trusting only Ko Win Naing's hands.

timeline.title: From CRT to the new screens
timeline.body: The bench changed with the sets. Ko Win Naing took on LED backlights, LCD boards, and the plasma displays other shops had begun to turn away, while the same families kept the shop.

timeline.title: North Okkalapa — New Home
timeline.body: Now operating near Maydar Wee Market (Maydarvi) in North Okkalapa township, serving an even wider community while preserving the same founding values: honesty, quality, and care.
